preamble: Spontaneous nasalization of a palatal sonorant: an initial palatal lateral (or the palatal that replaced it) is replaced by the palatal nasal [ɲ] while keeping its palatal place. Lipski (1992) identifies word-initial palatal > [ɲ] as a recurrent feature of Afro-Hispanic (bozal) Spanish texts and of contemporary dialects in regions with a strong African presence, most often in llamar > ñamar 'to call'. The change is sporadic and lexical, and in yeísta varieties the input may already have been [ʝ] rather than [ʎ]. Lipski notes the same shift with other palatals, as in chato > ñato.

examples.note: Lipski calls this the most frequent example of word-initial palatal > [ɲ] in Afro-Hispanic texts and in contemporary dialects of regions with a strong African presence.
Also cited by Lipski. The word comes from Quechua yapa, so the input palatal is not reliably [ʎ].

sources: Lipski, J. M. (1992). Spontaneous nasalization in the development of Afro-Hispanic language. Journal of Pidgin and Creole Languages, 7(2), 261–305. https://doi.org/10.1075/jpcl.7.2.04lip
